title: Refactor sampling policy to bounded-emission + low-overhead tail detection
creator: Maya Ortiz
description: Deliver a refactor of the tracing sampling layer to enforce a bounded span-emission budget per service while adding a low-cost tail-detection heuristic. Goal is to reduce CPU + network overhead from high-cardinality trace traffic without losing high-fidelity traces for tail latency and error analysis. This change should be safe for hosted and dedicated deployments, support config overrides per-customer, and include rollout/rollback tooling in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Bounded-emission policy implemented: each service can be configured with max_spans_per_second and burst_cap parameters
Low-cost tail detector implemented: inexpensive RT-percentile and error-rate trigger that temporarily bumps sampling for affected traces
End-to-end unit/ integration tests for deterministic sampling decisions and tail detector behavior
CPU and egress measurements show >=30% reduction in trace-related CPU and network for high-throughput workloads at default policy compared to current baseline
Canary rollout plan and automatic rollback hook implemented in Console
Docs updated: sampling policy reference and migration guide for existing customers
notes_and_updates: 2025-01-18: Ticket created after spike in production trace egress; initial proposal from Maya to explore bounded budgets + tail detector
2025-01-22: Spike analysis attached to Confluence and Grafana dashboard shows top 5 services responsible for 70% of span egress
2025-01-27: Prototype of bounded-emission developed by Ben; initial microbench shows 22% CPU improvement but higher false negatives for rare error spikes
2025-01-30: Added cheap tail heuristic: maintain 1-min running pct95 latency per route and mark candidate traces for temporary higher sampling when pct95 moves > 2x baseline
2025-02-02: Bench results: bounded policy + tail detector reduces trace CPU by 35% and preserves 92% of error-causing traces in synthetic fault injection test
2025-02-04: Design review with PM and Observability lead. Feedback: expose per-customer overrides, add audit log entry when policy escalates sampling, ensure KV-cache interactions are not impacted
2025-02-05: PR opened (see links). Integration tests failing intermittently around cross-service sampling inheritance; originating hypothesis: propagation headers being dropped in custom gateways
2025-02-06: Added short-term mitigation: fall back to deterministic hash sampling if propagation headers missing; next steps to fix gateway header propagation in ENG-10844
qa_plan: Unit tests for sampling decision math and tail detection thresholds
Integration test harness that replays production-like trace volume and validates span budget enforcement
Fault injection tests to ensure tail detector raises sampling for error bursts
Canary in staging with 10% traffic and real workloads for 72 hours before wider rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 0: deploy code behind feature flag to staging clusters
Phase 1: enable for non-critical internal services (10%) for 72h
Phase 2: enable for customer-facing services with monitoring alerts (25%)
Phase 3: gradual ramp to 100% with scheduled audits and automated rollback on elevated error/latency signals
tradeoffs_considered: Aggressive global sampling budgets reduce cost but risk losing rare error signals
Tail detector adds some state and computation but is designed to be amortized and kept per-route to limit memory
Per-customer overrides increase complexity but are required for enterprise customers with compliance needs
Using deterministic hash sampling as fallback preserves correlation for traces but may re-introduce some egress spikes for high-cardinality routes
